review: Independent read-only Rust WorldFeed HTTP/SSE and backend-selection review
verdict: FAIL CLOSED: transport gates pass, but independently reproduced HTML injection, unsafe roster-size validation and erased replay-gap provenance prevent approval.
evidence_level: Compiled Rust gates, offline current-Python serialization comparison, isolated actual Python FastAPI-to-Rust loopback, and independent Rust HTTP probes. NOT real game, AgentHost execution, Docker, browser/UI acceptance or durable replay proof.
scope: read-only Python wire contract in worldfeed_server.py/world_state.py

snapshot_drift.meaning: Parent's independent POP-001 lifecycle repair changed WorldState after the successful pinned loopback run. This report does not approve that new WorldState version, lifecycle synchronization, or host-bound safety under concurrency. The wire serializer itself remained hash-identical. Supplementary Python tests lack an atomic source hash capture and are not approval evidence for either WorldState lifecycle version.

security_concerns.finding: Editable upstream persona name is escaped in body text but inserted raw into the HTML title by shell(&detail.name,...). An accepted name containing a closing title plus script creates active script markup in the compiled live inspector response.
security_concerns.baseline: Raw title interpolation already existed in HEAD; the live adapter newly feeds Python-origin names into this unsafe sink. This is not claimed as a newly written escaping regression.
security_concerns.repro: On a fresh isolated WorldState, apply edit_persona for an existing persona with name </title><script>window.__review_xss=1</script><title>; serve create_app(state) on 127.0.0.1:0; launch compiled dashboard with WORLDFEED_URL pointing only to this reviewer-owned port; GET /agent/{persona_id}. Response contains the exact unescaped closing-title/script sequence. No browser execution was attempted.
security_concerns.suggested_resolution: Escape the title HTML context, and audit upstream strings in attitude, guild-goal, inline-JS persona ID and chat innerHTML sinks. Only the title exploit was exercised in this review.

security_concerns.finding: Live roster commands have no group, solo, per-group or total-agent upper bound. One million friend groups passes command_payload validation and is serialized for POST. In the reviewed Python version it reaches an unbounded SocietyRoster.build range(n_groups), so the adapter's response/body/cache caps do not bound upstream CPU/memory work. A three-second HTTP timeout cannot cancel already-running synchronous generation.
security_concerns.baseline: Missing bounds are inherited from mock command validation; forwarding to the Python process is the new live exposure. Latest parent lifecycle repair was not re-reviewed for this property.
security_concerns.repro: Offline only: command_payload(&Command::RegenerateRoster {seed:1,friend_groups:1_000_000,solos:0,friends_per_group_min:2,friends_per_group_max:2}) returns Ok. Do NOT send this to any WorldState server. Inspect the exact reviewed WorldState path and SocietyRoster.build's range(n_groups).
security_concerns.observed: MILLION_GROUPS_SERIALIZED=true; intentionally not posted or allocated
security_concerns.suggested_resolution: Define a bounded maximum population, use checked/widened total calculations, and reject oversized commands before any network request; maintain corresponding upstream safeguards.

logic_errors.finding: friend_groups + solos uses unchecked u32 addition before the empty-population test. Legal JSON u32 extrema panic in the debug-built command path rather than fail closed with CommandError; release wrapping also makes validation depend on build profile.
logic_errors.baseline: Unchecked addition exists in HEAD; newly reachable through the live command serialization path.
logic_errors.repro: Wrap command_payload(&Command::RegenerateRoster {seed:1,friend_groups:u32::MAX,solos:1,friends_per_group_min:2,friends_per_group_max:2}) in std::panic::catch_unwind in a Rust debug probe compiled against the gate's exact world_feed rlib.
logic_errors.observed: attempt to add with overflow at crates/world-feed/src/lib.rs:316:20; OVERFLOW_PANIC=true
logic_errors.execution_limit: Debug panic was exercised; release behavior was inferred from the unchecked expression, not run.

logic_errors.finding: Every successful SSE connection clears events_error, including unrecoverable replay-gap/restart warnings. A subsequent empty/comment-only reconnect erases evidence of missing IDs without any reconciliation or deliberate adapter restart. During that connection the current health logic can classify transport available despite the prior unrecoverable gap.
logic_errors.repro:
Isolated Rust axum upstream: first SSE response sends IDs 0 then 3; second response contains only ': connected

'. Call refresh, consume_events_once twice and inspect health after each. The missing 1/2 warning disappears after the second successful connection.
logic_errors.observed: First events_error='upstream replay gap; evicted events cannot be recovered'; second events_error=null, last_event_id=3. Both finite-response samples have events_status=disconnected. The connected available classification is a source-derived inference, not a browser or active-stream observation.
logic_errors.suggested_resolution: Separate persistent feed-integrity warnings from transient transport errors, clearing unrecoverable integrity warnings only through explicit reset/reconciliation.

rust_quality_gates.note: Most tests are mock/schema tests. Passing all gates is not a security review pass.

dashboard_build.command: nix develop -c cargo build --manifest-path dashboard/Cargo.toml -p dashboard-app

current_python_serializer_comparison.method: Regenerated deterministically in memory using the actual Python adapter, fixed clock and seed, and compared byte-for-byte. No fixture files were rewritten.

actual_python_loopback.host_binding_test_limit: Bound a private in-memory MemoryLog only; no AgentHost or game client ran, and no concurrent lifecycle-safety claim follows.
actual_python_loopback.after_owned_upstream_shutdown: stale health; cached roster HTTP 200 with x-worldfeed-status=stale

independent_rust_probe.method: Nix rustc links the successful gate's exact local world_feed, tokio, axum, futures_util and serde_json rlibs; every HTTP listener binds 127.0.0.1:0.

supplementary_python_tests.command: nix develop -c uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_worldfeed_server.py tests/test_worldfeed_retention.py tests/test_population_config.py -q
supplementary_python_tests.source_snapshot: Not atomically hash-pinned; concurrent parent WorldState repair means this is supplemental test evidence only, not lifecycle approval.

verified_contract_properties: Absent backend environment selects live; unknown mode fails configuration; only explicit mock branch creates synthetic ticker. Dead upstream remains live/unavailable and does not supply fake agents/events.

Python wire DTOs preserve memory strings, character names, level-band, goal/script/plan and separate reputation scores; missing numeric fields are nullable and absent textual fields marked not supplied; source summaries are not reclassified as observed game actions.
Existing Rust tests exercise arbitrary LF/CRLF chunk boundaries, partial-frame withholding, 128 KiB frame bound, Last-Event-ID resume and duplicate suppression.
Snapshot/command deadlines are present, redirects/proxies disabled, HTTP bodies and roster bounded; independent probes additionally exercised body, roster and broadcast bounds.
Detail network operations are async; code inspection shows ten-second default TTL and 128-entry oldest-cache eviction. Exhaustive cache-eviction/TTL execution was not completed.

Supported edit commands flatten correctly; generation renames groups/solos/bounds correctly against the pinned Python contract; singleton friend-size and host-bound generation failures remain failures.

Unsupported force actions and schedule-bearing edits reject before upstream mutation. Successful supported POST acknowledgements are Python source events labeled WorldState-only, not AgentHost application or game execution.
accepted_explicit_exclusions: Numeric upstream IDs are process-lifetime, not epochs: lower IDs after restart are suppressed and an intentional adapter restart is required; no automatic epoch recovery promised.
Evicted upstream history is unrecoverable; downstream bounded broadcast has no durable replay and skips lagged receivers.
Static roster/inspector reload requirement; LiveView auto-polls cached roster/health.
No real game, host-worker, Docker, provider, credentials, shared-service or SQL acceptance.
limitations_and_issues_encountered: Initial reviewer harness shutdown waited on an infinite SSE request. Successful rerun used a reviewer-only bounded uvicorn graceful shutdown; expected CancelledError logged, all owned processes terminated.

An expanded cache/streaming-body/malformed-SSE follow-up was blocked by the execution tool's no-consent timeout. It was not retried or routed through another tool; no claimed execution for those added checks. Scratch probe was restored to its previously executed version.
WorldState changed after successful pinned run; no approval across that drift. The new POP-001 repair and protocol L3-TEMP review are separate workstreams, not resolved here.
No browser was opened. HTML-injection markup was observed in an HTTP response, not a browser-executed exploit or rendered UI acceptance.
No adversarial million-agent generation was posted; resource risk is supported by offline serialization plus the exact reviewed unbounded upstream implementation.
suggestions: Preserve safe, bounded upstream 400 details rather than returning only generic HTTP status, so friend-size/host-bound rejections are actionable without pretending success.
README and implementation report population-imperfection statements lag the reviewed Python count/bound fixes; describe current pinned behavior and keep lifecycle safety separate.
